subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Safety Culture: The Invisible Shield
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Safety Culture: The Invisible Shield.

hook.text: A strong safety culture catches problems before they become disasters. A weak one suppresses warnings until it's too late.

buildup.text: In a strong safety culture, any worker can stop a process if they spot a hazard. Reporting near-misses is rewarded, not punished.

discovery.text: NASA's culture before Challenger normalized deviance — small anomalies were accepted until abnormal became the new normal.

twist.text: Alcoa's CEO made worker safety his top priority in 1987. The company became both the safest and most profitable aluminum maker.

climax.text: High-reliability organizations like aircraft carriers and nuclear plants maintain safety through constant vigilance and training.

punchline.text: Safety isn't a rule. It's a culture. And culture saves lives.

quiz.question: What is normalization of deviance in engineering safety?
options: Deliberately lowering safety standards to reduce manufacturing costs
Gradually accepting small anomalies until abnormal conditions become the new normal
Training workers to deviate from standard procedures in emergencies
